questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: First of all it is cheaper in man cases. Further you do not have to follow dorm guidelines. Lastly you meet a lot of different people with very different backgrounds.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything worked out and I got the required amount of credits. Nevertheless the course registration period it stressfull and difficult if you have not familiarized yourself with the system beforehand. I ended up personally contacting the professors of some courses to secure a spot on the course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a bidding system where you have a total amount of points of which you can bid a certain amount of each course you wish to have. After this there is an add drop period where students can cancel their registration which will open up more seats.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We received emails with guidance from the university. Further they were fast to reply when emailing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got 3 out of 5 courses. But I secured a spot on the last two courses by writing directly to the professors who was teaching the courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a plan beforehand for what you will do and make sure to familiarize yourself with the system.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a limited amount of courses but the courses were interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was easier

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more of student participation was required a large part of the final grade was decided by your participation in class. The professors will also cold call you if you do not participate. This actually creates a dynamic style of teaching where it is possible to have class discussions even though the classes was online.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Comparative corporate law and  governance. The professor was great and was mostly just functioning as a moderator of the class discussion with only a small amount of an actual lecture. We were only 7 students in class all from different countries which made it possible to have very good class discussions.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around Korea. Visit other big cities such as Busan or visit the DMZ. Further you should spend a lot of time in Seoul. It is one of the worlds biggest cities and there will always be new areas for you to discover. Personally I enjoyd hiking in the mountain areas within Seoul and visiting museums or just visiting different neighborhoods.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. There are a lot of exchange students who are in the same position as you are and therefore it is very easy to make new friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open minded and go out a lot! Do not be afraid to talk to strangers. Further make sure to get contact informations on the people you meet - Seoul is a big city and chances of you running into them again randomly is small.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of Koreans are not good in English which made it difficult to socialize with the locals. However those who are comfortable speaking English are very kind and helpfull.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality from the Koreans! They are all very helpfull and wishes for you to enjoy your stay in their country which made it a very nice environment to be in.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to do a lot of research before going. It will give you a big advantage when choosing courses and finding housing. 

2. Be outgoing and do not be afraid to talk to new people. There is a lot of exchange students who also just arrived and is in the exact same situation as you are in so it is in everybody's interest. 

3. If you have to go to quarantine due to covid, give priority to find a good apartment to do the quarantine in. 14 days is a lot in the same room, and if you pick a cheap place you can easily end up with a small room with only a mattress and no windows. Do not use the quarantine services but instead book a nice apartment and make sure to do your research on how to order food and groceries before going. Further make sure to buy some bottles of water and some food in the airport to get you through the first days if something doesn't work out for you in the beginning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The privilege of being able to live in another part of the world and all the new friends from countries all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: When arriving in the airport not knowing anything and going straight to a quarantine apartment where I had to figure out how to order food and water.

questions.answer: Yes
